summary: Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Paul Pelliot (~1939–1945) and at Cambridge (~1948). He held posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University (Director 1962–1986; Series Editor ~1960–2000).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at SOAS (1946–1947) and St Catharine's College (~1947–1950). He held posts at London (1954–1968), Cambridge (1956–1960; Chair of Chinese 1968–1980), and Princeton (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. She studied at the École des chartes (~1942–1947) and the École des langues orientales (~1946–1950), later serving on the faculty of INALCO from ~1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Drepung Loseling and Gyume Tantric Monastery under teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, he served as principal at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1967–1976) and abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991).
Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

Dennis Genpo Merzel (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of Southern California (~1962–1966), USC Rossier School of Education (~1966–1968), and under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (~1972–1995).

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies. Educated at UC Berkeley (BA ~1963–1967; MA ~1967–1969) and Nagoya University (PhD ~1992–1996), he held positions at Hongwanji International Center (~1976–1995), Ryukoku University (~1996–2017), and Harvard (2008).

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1946–1950). He held posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1958–1988) and Iryo Sosei University.

Derek F. Maher specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia (PhD 2003 under Jeffrey Hopkins), he has taught at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. His academic career included posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968), Newcastle University (1970–2005), and the University of Vienna (2008).

Dermott Walsh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin (-2003), an MA at Leiden University (-2009), and a PhD at UCLA (-2018) under the supervision of William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917) and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910).
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).
Dezhung Kunga Gyaltsen was a scholar who pursued his studies under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khenpo Shenga.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Gaton Ngawang Lekpa and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse. He was a research project participant at the University of Washington from 1960 to 1972.

Dharmananda Damodar Kosambi (1876–1947) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard (1926). He held academic posts at Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard (~1910–1931), Gujarat University (~1920–1925), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1930).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1920–1936) and held academic posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma is a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under teachers David Friedman and Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He served as an associate lecturer at Open University (attested 2017) and held a post at the University of Chester (2019).

Di Luo is a scholar of sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA and by Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge for a PhD, Luo studied at the University of Southern California (attested 2016).
